html:
The Sauk and the Meskwaki (also called the Fox) are two closely related Algonquian peoples of the western Great Lakes. The map shows them in 1492 on the upper Mississippi, between Iowa and Illinois, where they lived from the 1700s; earlier they lived further east, around Michigan and Wisconsin.

The Meskwaki fought the French in the Fox Wars of 1712 to the 1730s, and the Sauk took them in, binding the two together. They lived in summer farming towns and winter hunting camps. In 1804 a few Sauk leaders signed away their lands east of the Mississippi in a treaty that others never accepted. In 1832 Black Hawk led a band back to Illinois, starting the Black Hawk War, which ended in a massacre at the Bad Axe River.

Their descendants are the Sac and Fox Nation of Oklahoma, the Sac and Fox of Missouri, and the Meskwaki of Iowa, who bought back their own land at Tama in 1857. See also Sauk and Meskwaki.
